title.en: Electron emission and the photoelectric effect

hook.en: Automatic doors and solar calculators rely on one fact: light can pull *electrons* out of a metal. But electrons are held inside by the metal. What frees them?

say.en: Automatic doors and solar calculators rely on one fact: light can pull electrons out of a metal. But electrons are held inside by the metal. What frees them? In this lesson: Define work function.

body.en: Free electrons in a metal are held back by the attraction of the positive ions at the surface. The minimum energy an electron needs to escape is the *work function* $\phi_0$, usually given in electron volts ($1$ eV $= 1.6\times10^{-19}$ J). The energy can be supplied by heat (thermionic emission), by a very strong electric field (field emission), or by light (photoelectric emission).
body.kn: ಲೋಹದಿಂದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಹೊರಬರಲು ಬೇಕಾದ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಶಕ್ತಿಯೇ ಕಾರ್ಯಫಲನ φ₀. ಶಾಖ (ಉಷ್ಣಅಯಾನಿಕ ಉತ್ಸರ್ಜನೆ), ಪ್ರಬಲ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ (ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಉತ್ಸರ್ಜನೆ) ಅಥವಾ ಬೆಳಕು (ದ್ಯುತಿವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಉತ್ಸರ್ಜನೆ) ಈ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ನೀಡಬಹುದು.

title.en: Board: getting electrons out of a metal

narration.en: Let us see what holds electrons inside a metal and how much energy frees them.

say.en: A metal has free electrons, but they cannot leave the surface on their own: the positive ions pull them back.
The least energy needed to pull the most energetic electron out is the work function, φ₀.
That energy can come from heat, from a very strong electric field, or from light. With light it is the photoelectric effect.
Work functions are a few electron-volts. Light can free electrons only if its wavelength is shorter than 1240 divided by φ₀ in eV, in nanometres. For sodium that is about 451 nm.
Let us see what holds electrons inside a metal and how much energy frees them.

narration.en: Each photon carries energy hν. If hν is more than the work function φ0 of the metal, an electron can escape with kinetic energy up to hν − φ0. Below the threshold frequency nothing comes out, however bright the light. Brighter light (same ν) only frees more electrons.
narration.kn: ಬೆಳಕು ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊರಹಾಕುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

caption.en: Each photon carries energy hν. If hν is more than the work function φ0 of the metal, an electron can escape with kinetic energy up to hν − φ0. Below the threshold frequency nothing comes out, however bright the light. Brighter light (same ν) only frees more electrons.
caption.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಫೋಟಾನ್ hν ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ. hν ಲೋಹದ ಕಾರ್ಯ ಫಲನ φ0 ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದ್ದರೆ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ hν − φ0 ವರೆಗಿನ ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊರಬರುತ್ತದೆ. ಆರಂಭ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಗಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಎಷ್ಟೇ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನ ಬೆಳಕಿದ್ದರೂ ಏನೂ ಹೊರಬರದು. ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತೀವ್ರತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಮಾತ್ರ.

body.en: Hertz (1887) noticed that sparks jumped more easily when ultraviolet light fell on the electrodes. Hallwachs and Lenard found that ultraviolet light on a zinc plate releases negative charges, later identified as *electrons*. Zinc and cadmium need ultraviolet light, but alkali metals like sodium, potassium and caesium respond even to visible light. For each metal there is a threshold frequency below which nothing happens.
body.kn: ಹರ್ಟ್ಸ್, ಹಾಲ್‌ವಾಕ್ಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಲೆನಾರ್ಡ್ ನೇರಳಾತೀತ ಬೆಳಕು ಲೋಹದಿಂದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊರಹಾಕುವುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡರು. ಕ್ಷಾರ ಲೋಹಗಳು ದೃಗ್ಗೋಚರ ಬೆಳಕಿಗೂ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಲೋಹಕ್ಕೂ ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ ಇದೆ.

heading.en: Electron Emission and the Photoelectric Effect

tagline.en: Work function, the three ways to free electrons from a metal, and what the photoelectric experiment shows about intensity, frequency and stopping potential.

myth.en: If I use brighter light, the photoelectrons come out with more kinetic energy.

truth.en: Brighter light of the same frequency gives more photoelectrons per second, but the same maximum kinetic energy. In everyday life a stronger push means a faster object, so this feels natural. But each electron absorbs one photon, and a photon's energy is fixed by frequency.

title.en: The experiment and its three results

say.en: An evacuated glass tube has a photosensitive plate C (emitter) and a collector plate A. Monochromatic light enters through a quartz window and falls on C.
Wave theory says a brighter wave carries more energy, so the electrons should come out faster. Wave theory says any frequency should work if the light is bright enough or shines long enough.

goal.en: Work function, the three ways to free electrons from a metal, and what the photoelectric experiment shows about intensity, frequency and stopping potential.

task.en: What does each quantity depend on?

explain.en: Intensity controls how many electrons come out per second. Frequency controls whether they come out and how fast the fastest ones move.

question.en: The intensity of light on a photocell is doubled, keeping the frequency fixed. What happens to the stopping potential?

explain.en: Stopping potential depends only on frequency and the metal. Doubling intensity doubles the saturation current, not $V_0$.

takeaway.en: Work function $\phi_0$ is the minimum energy needed to free an electron from a metal surface; $1\ \text{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J.

narration.en: Many people think: If I use brighter light, the photoelectrons come out with more kinetic energy. Actually: Brighter light of the same frequency gives more photoelectrons per second, but the same maximum kinetic energy. In everyday life a stronger push means a faster object, so this feels natural. But each electron absorbs one photon, and a photon's energy is fixed by frequency.

problem.en: The work function of caesium is 2.14 eV. Express it in joules.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The work function of caesium is 2.14 eV. Express it in joules.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The work function of caesium is 2.14 electron volts. Express it in joules.
phi 0 equals 2.14 times 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
phi 0 is approximately 3.42 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
So the answer is is approximately 3.4 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
